title: Inter-team Canary Cessation & Reintegration Protocol (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This note defines an operational protocol for safe, low-friction stopping (cessation) of a canary cohort that spans multiple teams, and a clear path to reintegrate traffic once signals are acceptable. Focus is operational choreography: who does what, what telemetry gates to check, and templated comms to reduce reaction-time during incidents.

Context / Why this exists:
We run many progressive activations where feature logic, model routing, and client-side flags cross team boundaries. When a canary starts causing degraded user experience we often have friction deciding: pause traffic? re-route? rollback model? let the canary run longer? The goal is to reduce decision latency and avoid unnecessary full rollbacks for interdependent features.

Scope / out-of-scope:
- In scope: multi-team canaries involving routing, model variants, and console-driven traffic slices. Covers immediate cessation steps, short-term mitigation, and structured reintegration.
- Out of scope: post-incident RCA process (handled in incident-runbooks), compliance/legal escalation, or infrastructure-level capacity failures unrelated to feature logic.

Definitions (quick):
- Cessation: intentional, controlled stop or reduction of traffic to the canary cohort (0% or a smaller %).
- Reintegration: staged restoration of traffic to the canary cohort after checks pass.
- Guardrail signals: automated telemetry thresholds that must be cleared before reintegration (latency, error-rate, quality signals).

Roles (who to call / tag):
- Canary Owner (CO): feature/product PM who owns hypothesis and rollout plan.
- Routing Owner (RO): infra/serving engineer responsible for routing changes and canary slice config.
- Oncall SRE (SRE): responsible for cluster health and coordinating rollbacks if infra fails.
- Observability Lead (OBS): person who validates telemetry, constructs emergency queries, and confirms signal baselines.
- Incident Communicator (IC): person to craft and send status updates to stakeholders.

Quick decision flow (one-liner):
1) If high-sev signal -> Cessation (RO executes slice quiesce), CO + SRE + OBS stand up sync.
2) Mitigate (fallback model / route to baseline) if available.
3) Observe for minimum quiesce window (15 minutes) and validate guardrail signals.
4) Reintegration as staged ramp if safe; otherwise revert to rollback plan.

Cessation checklist (immediate steps - checklist for RO/CO/SRE):
- [ ] Tag oncall and create temporary channel (Slack #canary-emergency-xxxx).
- [ ] RO: pause or reduce canary slice to 0% (if immediate), or to safe floor (example 0.1%). Document exact command executed and timestamp.
- [ ] RO: enable forced routing to baseline model/variant for affected user cohorts.
- [ ] SRE: confirm cluster health and that cessation did not create cascading resource pressure.
- [ ] OBS: run smoke queries (list below) and confirm error-rate/latency delta vs baseline. Capture screenshots/links to dashboard.
- [ ] CO: post hypothesis and short note in channel: what changed, expected effect, and quick recovery plan.

Minimum quiesce window and rationale:
- Standard quiesce window: 15 minutes (short instability). For behavior regressions that affect quality metrics (e.g., content moderation hits or hallucination scoring) use 60–120 minutes to capture downstream user feedback signals.
- Rationale: short windows limit user damage and give telemetry time to stabilize. Longer windows for quality regressions because downstream pipelines and human review signals can lag.

Telem gates (guardrails for reintegration) — every gate must be true for at least two consecutive windows (5m windows recommended):
- API error rate (5xx) for canary cohort <= baseline + 0.2% absolute AND not trending upwards.
- 95th latency for key endpoints <= baseline 95th + 150ms (absolute) for latency-sensitive features.
- Quality/regression signals: human-reviewed sample pass-rate within 1.5x baseline failure rate (if applicable).
- Business KPI sanity: conversion/success-rate for critical flows within acceptable drift (team-specific).
- No new alert fires with severity >= P2 attributable to the canary.

Reintegration plan (ramp strategy):
- Phase 0: Validation & Dry-run (after cessation but before traffic ramp) — run shadow traffic to new variant for 30–60 minutes; verify telemetry. Shadow does not affect users but exercises code paths.
- Phase 1: Micro-ramp — restore to 1–5% for 10–20 minutes. Run telem gates.
- Phase 2: Gradual doubling (x2 every 15–30 minutes) with active observability checks until target exposure.
- Phase 3: Full restoration and post-restore watch (2 hours at target).
- Abort criteria at any phase: any guardrail violation or human-sensed regression -> immediate cessation and postmortem entry.

Communication templates (short snippets to paste):
- Immediate slack post (IC):
  "[SEV] Canary pause: paused canary slice for feature <X> at 2025-02-12T14:38Z. CO: @Maya, RO: @Liam. Observability team running checks. Creating incident channel #canary-emergency-233. Please do not re-enable traffic without triage'"
- Reintegration notice (IC):
  "Starting reintegration: Phase 1 (1% micro-ramp) for feature <X>. Expected duration 20m. Watch: dashboard://console/rollouts/canary-health and logs://query/quick-check. Contact: @Priya for signal questions."

Quick smoke queries (OBS shortcuts to run after pause):
- errors_by_route(canary) vs errors_by_route(baseline) last 30m
- p95_latency(key-endpoint, canary) vs baseline last 30m
- moderation_failures(sample) last 60m (if relevant)
- sampling of user sessions with canary tag for manual review (limit 50)

Reintegration caveats and team-specific exceptions:
- If reintegration requires client SDK changes, coordinate with SDK team and increase guardrail window to 2x.
- For experiments affecting billing/monetization funnels use business KPI gates and CC revenue owner.
- For private deployment customers (Private mode) use customer-specific rollback playbook and notify compliance manager.

Post-action artifacts (what to capture for the runbook/RCA):
- Timestamped list of routing commands executed (RO).
- Links/screenshots of dashboards used, smoke query results (OBS).
- Decision log: who decided to cease, who approved reintegration, and why.
- Short blameless postmortem draft in :confluence:CR-2382 within 48 hours.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- TODO: add a small automation to run the telem gates post-cessation and publish PASS/FAIL boolean to the incident channel. (Owner: Priya)
- TODO: standardize the quiesce window per experiment type (quality vs infra). Current doc uses heuristics; propose explicit matrix.
- Question: should we have an automated half-life ramp (e.g., exponential decay) vs doubling? Simpler doubling is easier to reason about but less conservative.
- TODO: script snippet for RO to create an immutable audit record of routing change (CLI command + git-backed record).

Appendix — quick notes from a rehearsal (lab log):
- 2025-01-27: rehearsal with Payments team. Pause executed in 45s. Shadow validation flagged duplicate-charge edge-case at 12m. Good to have 30–60m window for financial flows.
- Behavioural learnings: channels with clear named roles allowed faster decisions. When roles were fuzzy we lost 8–12 minutes.

End notes:
This is intentionally pragmatic and incomplete. The purpose is to reduce friction for the first 60 minutes of a cross-team canary issue. Pull requests to add automation hooks, sample queries, and explicit per-team gate thresholds encouraged.

-- Maya (draft, notes to self)
